Subject: ACME TCO recap & next steps (batching/caching options)

Hi Priya & Jordan,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to walk through the ACME ingestion pipeline and cost concerns. TL;DR from our side and proposed next steps below.

Pain points you shared:
- High monthly token spend driven by long-context customer transcripts + multi-turn summarization (~120M tokens/mo).
- Embeddings workload (semantic search) is high-concurrency and driving steady-state spend.
- Tight procurement budget this cycle; primary goal is to reduce month-over-month inference cost by ~30-40% without materially degrading user experience.
- Latency SLOs: 95th p95 target ~200ms for chat flows; embeddings can tolerate higher latency (<= 1s).

Redwood cost levers we discussed (high-level):
1) Batching: continuous/auto-batching on dedicated pools can reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead by ~20-40% depending on concurrency patterns.
2) Prefix/KV caching: for repeat prompts and multi-turn chat, prefix caching can cut effective tokens billed by avoiding regeneration of unchanged prefix content.
3) Model variant + quantization: 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants can lower GPU cost; combined with batching yields additional savings.
4) Routing policy: route lower-priority work (embeddings or background summarization) to cost-optimized nodes or off-peak windows.
5) Dedicated capacity vs hosted bursts: an upfront reserved pool can bring predictable unit economics for high-volume workloads.

Immediate next steps we propose:
- I attached a starter TCO workbook (ACME_TCO_model_v1.xlsx) with a baseline estimate and scenarios for batching/caching and quantized models.
- Quick SE deep-dive next week to map your infra telemetry to realistic batching assumptions (30-45 min).
- If the TCO looks reasonable, propose a 6-8 week pilot on a dedicated pool with measurable cost/regression SLIs.

Action items: 
- Rafael: share TCO workbook + a one-pager (attached) with redwood assumptions. (done)
- ACME: share last 3 months of token counts (monthly), embedding QPS, and current costs if possible so we can refine numbers.
- Schedule: can we target a SE call next Tue/Wed?

Thanks — happy to jump on another call to walk through the workbook live.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Thanks Priya — and appreciated the target budget. Quick follow-up with some back-of-envelope numbers so you have a sense before we refine with your telemetry: 

Back-of-envelope / sample economics (baseline assumptions)
- Baseline model: 1.3B decoder (~cost proxy) — baseline hosted inference: $0.30 per 1k tokens.
- 120M tokens/mo -> baseline cost = (120,000 * $0.30) = $36,000/mo (matches your ~35k/m).

Savings scenarios (examples):
- Add continuous batching + reserved pool: 25% unit reduction -> $27,000/mo.
- Add prefix/KV caching on chat flows (assume 30% of tokens avoid regeneration): additional effective reduction -> $20,000/mo.
- Replace some high-volume flows with quantized variant: further ~10-15% -> target ~$17-18k/mo.

We attached the workbook (ACME_TCO_model_v1.xlsx) that encodes these scenarios; the first tab is a baseline, second tab has batching/caching/quantization scenarios. I also attached a short PDF with our standard pilot terms and estimated SLA for dedicated pools.

I'll also add procurement@acme.com and sec_ops@acme.com to the loop after you confirm.

Best,
Rafael
